description: Sub-division of site and erection of a single storey dwelling for 2 x  residential units, cycle, waste and recycling storage areas and soft landscaping.
subdivision_of_building: Rear Garden of existing property with communal use of front garden.
decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice.Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans: BNG_101BNG_A103BNG_A102A105A106A107A103A101A104A102A100_1 REV AA100_2 REV ABIODIVERSITY NET GAIN REPORTFlood Risk and Surface Water Assessment Rev0Internal Daylight and Sunlight StudySunlight and Overshadowing StudyDesign Stage Water Efficiency Report Part GTransport Technical NoteTrees and ConstructionBS5837:2012 Tree Survey, Arboricultural Impact Assessment & Method StatementEnergy StatementReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

Prior to the commencement of above ground works of the development hereby permitted, details including detailed drawings (at 1:20 and 1:5) and photographs of samples to be used in the external elevations shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall thereafter be built in accordance with the approved details. The following details are required:a)	External facing materials including manufacturer specification of all facing materials and finishes including windows and door openings including frame and window bars (minimum reveal depth 1 brick / 215mm),a 1:20 bay study elevation, section and plan to include bay and dormer windows;b)	Refuse store, cycle store and rainwater goods;c)	Brickwork (bespoke 1m x 1m physical sample panel constructed on site for officer review (inc. bond, joint and mortar); d)	Soft and hard landscaping including access paths, permeable paving, gates, communal areas and boundary treatment;e)	Green Sedum roof (cycle store), ASHP enclosure, inc. installation fixings and screening;f)	External lighting.Reason: To ensure the external appearance of the building is satisfactory and that it protects the character and appearance of the surrounding area.

Notwithstanding the details set out in the submitted Preliminary Drainage Strategy (Flood Risk and Surface Water Assessment Rev0) 28 May 2026, prior to the commencement of above-ground works, detailed design and construction information for the surface water drainage strategy hereby approved shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The details shall be in general accordance with the submitted Flood Risk and Surface Water Assessment Rev1 and SuDS Pro Forma, and shall include:a) confirmation of the final surface water drainage layout, including all SuDS features to be provided on site;b) final discharge rates and supporting calculations for the 1 in 1 year and 1 in 100 year storm events, including an appropriate allowance for climate change, together with evidence that runoff rates have been reduced as close to greenfield rates as reasonably practicable;c) details of the final runoff destination and evidence demonstrating compliance with the London Plan drainage hierarchy, including justification where infiltration is not feasible;d) finished floor levels and site levels in relation to the modelled flood risk, including confirmation that the development will be safe from flooding and will not increase flood risk elsewhere;e) details of exceedance flow routing and the means by which flows in excess of the design event will be safely managed on site or directed away from buildings;f) detailed drawings, sections, sizing and specifications for all drainage features, including permeable paving, flow controls, pipework, attenuation storage and any rainwater harvesting features;g) details of water quality treatment measures and how the drainage strategy follows the SuDS management train, where reasonably practicable;h) details of the ownership, management and maintenance arrangements for the lifetime of the development.The approved drainage works shall be implemented in full in accordance with the approved details and retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD Policy 61, and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan and the NPPF and to maximise opportunities for sustainable development, improve water quality, biodiversity, local amenity and recreation value.

The development hereby permitted shall be implemented in accordance with Energy statement (Dated: 19 February 2026) submitted with this application and shall ensure that the energy saving referenced in the report are achieved.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

5b Following practical completion of works a final Energy Performance Certificate with accompanying Building Regulations compliance report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Where applicable, a Display Energy Certificate shall be submitted within 18 months following first occupation.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The development must achieve reduced water consumption through the use of water efficient fittings, appliances and recycling systems to result in consumption equal to or less than 105 litres per person per day.Reason: To promote water conservation and efficiency measures in all new developments and where possible in the retrofitting of existing stock in accordance with Core Policy 21 of the Core Strategy and the London Plan

Prior to commencement of any development, a construction management plan must be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The construction management plan shall be written in accordance with London Best Practice Guidance and contain:a. A photographic condition survey of the public roads, footways and verges leading to the site.b. Details of construction access and associated traffic management.c. Arrangements for the loading, unloading and turning of delivery,construction and service vehicles.d. Arrangements for the parking of contractors' vehicles.e. Arrangements for wheel cleaning.f. Arrangements for the storage of materials.g. Hours of work.h. The storage and removal of excavation material.i. Measures to reduce danger to cyclists.j. Dust mitigation measures written in accordance with the Mayor of London's supplementary planning guidance 'The Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition' detailing how dust and emissions will be managed during demolition and construction worksk. Membership of the Considerate Contractors SchemeThe development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved construction management plan unless otherwise agreed by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure construction does not lead to damage of the nearby public road network and to minimise disruption to the neighbouring properties.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015, or any amending Order, no buildings or extensions to buildings, windows, or doors other than those indicated on the approved drawings shall be installed in the development hereby approved without the approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To safeguard the privacy of the occupiers of adjoining properties

No above ground works shall commence until details of hard and soft landscaping, including details of trees, shrubs and grass to be planted on the site have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The planting scheme shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details in the first planting season after completion or occupation of the development whichever is the sooner. Any planting which dies, becomes severely damaged or diseased within five years of planting shall be replaced with new planting in accordance with the approved details.REASON: To ensure that the proposed development does not prejudice the appearance of the locality and to preserve and enhance nature conservation interests.

The development shall not be occupied until details of the siting, number and design of secure/covered 4 cycle parking spaces have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved details shall thereafter be installed and permanently retained for cycle parking.Reason: The Council's Climate Action and Transport Policies seek to increase the use of active and sustainable transport modes. This means that access to bicycle parking should be easy and secure to remove potential barriers to cycling.

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the future number of occupiers on site have been provided within the development, in accordance with the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024). Such facilities to be retained permanently thereafter.Reason: To safeguard the amenity of the occupiers of adjoining premises; protect the general environment; prevent any obstruction to pedestrian movement and to ensure that there are adequate facilities for the storage and recycling of recoverable materials.

Prior to commencement of above ground works, the means of site enclosure, inclusive of the rear private gardens, must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved details shall be installed prior to occupation and remain in perpetuity.Reason: In the interests of highway safety and maintaining adequate visual clearance and privacy.

The development hereby approved, shall be completed in accordance with the BS5837:2012 Tree Survey, Arboricultural Impact Assessment & Method Statement prepared by Indigo Surveys dated June 2026, unless otherwise agreed by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure the adequate protection of the trees and in the interests of biodiversity.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including all preparatory work), a full specification and design for the foundations shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The specification shall demonstrate adherence to the guidelines set out in NHBC Chapter 4.2 Building near Trees.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority ensure that off site trees of high amenity value and public benefit will not be at risk through implication in possible future subsidence cases, in accordance with Policy DMD80(b) (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Prior to the commencement of above ground works, details of the siting and number of bat bricks/tiles and bird bricks/tubes/boxes and any other appropriate ecological enhancements shall be designed into and around the new buildings and trees, under the supervision of a suitably qualified ecologist, and shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Confirmation of installation, prior to first occupation, together with accompanying photographic evidence shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To enhance the site post development provides suitable nesting features for birds and bats.
